Hi team —

We have David Hart at final stage (Greenhouse link below). Emma needs final packaging guidance for a remote offer. Candidate is US-based (Portland) but is open to relocating to Ireland (EU) or Singapore (APAC) depending on visa speed. We need clear guidance on:

- Base bands to propose per region (US remote vs Ireland vs Singapore)
- Whether to include a COLA supplement or fixed locality multiplier for EU/APAC
- Any payroll / benefits caveats (stock grant vesting alignment, tax gross-up notes)

I've attached a draft pay grid and the candidate offer stub. High-level constraints: headcount is approved for IC3 SWE on the org chart; budget runway wants total comp under $220k USD equivalent if possible.

Can you confirm recommended ranges and whether we should present a single global offer with location-adjusted annex, or explicit region-specific offers? Quick replies are fine — Emma will send the formal PDF once we lock numbers.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 9:15 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> We have David Hart at final stage (Greenhouse link below). Emma needs final packaging guidance for a remote offer. Candidate is US-based (Portland) but is open to relocating to Ireland (EU) or Singapore (APAC) depending on visa speed.

Thanks Steph. My quick take (keeping total comp target <= $220k USD equivalent):

- US remote (Portland): Base $150,000 — $160,000; target OTE with equity (RSUs) + 401k matching to land around $190k—$205k depending on grant band. No COLA.
- Ireland (Dublin): Convert to EUR at current FX; recommend base €135,000 — €145,000 (approx. $145k—$156k USD) and a location supplement of €6k as a discretionary COLA for cost-of-living + payroll overheads. That keeps total comp near US-equivalent while reflecting employer tax burden.
- Singapore: Base SGD 190,000 — 205,000 with a fixed locality allowance SGD 8k — 12k (one-time relocation/settling allowance) — payroll burden is significant, so keep equity proportion slightly lower and increase cash to meet local expectations.

Operational notes:
- Presenting a single global offer with a regional annex is cleaner: core role, level, and vesting identical; annex spells out pay components and any statutory benefits per country.
- Finance should confirm tax withholding / employer social contributions for Ireland and Singapore before sign.
- If candidate stays in US but intends to travel/temporarily work abroad, include a clause that pay will be adjusted if permanent relocation occurs.

If you want, I can draft the three annex templates for the offer PDF.

-Markus
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 10:02 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> If you want, I can draft the three annex templates for the offer PDF.

Please do — that's the fastest path. A couple quick governance points from payroll/comp:

- If we include a recurring COLA for EU hires, we need a policy note (annual review cadence) so hiring managers don't expect arbitrary increases.
- For Ireland specifically, confirm whether we classify David as Irish payroll (local contract) or as remote worker with employer registration — that impacts gross-up and employer PRSI.
- For Singapore, coordinate with GSO (our vendor) early on benefits enrollment timeline — medical and CPF equivalents differ.

Approve the recommended ranges above as a starting point. Finance should sign off on the final amount; Markus, can you mark the final approved USD-equivalent ceiling?

Laura Bennett
Head of Talent Operations
